messages:
sara: Quick thread  LargeBank wants a 2-week POC where all customer data and logs must remain in Germany. They asked whether hosted API can be made acceptable or if we must push Dedicated/Private. Need a short answer + config and rough cost delta.

diego: Quick take: hosted can usually meet region residency if we pin to eu-central-1 and disable outbound analytics. Caveat: shared control plane metadata (account-level routing decisions) may be stored in other regions unless explicitly configured for enterprise.

maria: Legal note: we can share our sub-processor inventory and SOC reports. However if the customers compliance team requires zero third-party processors, only Private on-prem will qualify. Otherwise Hosted + contractual data processing terms + enterprise opt-outs should be fine.

sara: They specifically asked: (a) any user-identifying telemetry that might leave DE? (b) could model fallback ever go to non-EU region during the POC?

diego: (a) By default billing events are routed to our billing service in eu-central; usage aggregation sometimes pipelines for analytics. For the POC we can opt out so telemetry stays in-region and retained per EU policy. (b) Fallback: our smart router defaults to same-region compatible variants. Cross-region fallback only occurs when capacity is exhausted and the routing policy allows it. For the POC we can set allow_cross_region_failover=false.

samir: Operational option: spin a small Dedicated pool in eu-central for the POC. That ensures instance-level isolation and KMS in eu-central. I'll stand up 2x small GPUs for the 2-week window if they want guaranteed throughput.

sara: Cost question: customer expects low traffic (~60 short requests/min). Can you ballpark Dedicated reservation vs hosted with strict regional pin?

diego: Ballpark numbers: Hosted (with enterprise opt-outs) ~ standard per-token pricing; minor surcharge for regional egress policies (~+5-12%). Small Dedicated reservation for 2x A10G equivalent ~ $11k-$14k/mo committed, plus lower per-token compute for reserved capacity. For very low volume, hosted usually ends up cheaper; Dedicated makes sense for SLAs or strict isolation.

maria: Subprocessors I'll disclose for EU-only config: AWS (eu-central), Datadog EU logs, ElasticSearch (EU cluster option), Sentry (EU retention), PagerDuty, Stripe (billing). I'll attach CSV and DPA clauses.

sara: Can we give them the exact minimal config to enforce the residency constraints?

diego: Paste this snippet in the runbook for them:

```json
{
  "routing_policy": "regional_pin",
  "preferred_region": "eu-central-1",
  "allow_cross_region_failover": false,
  "telemetry_export": "disabled",
  "kms_key_region": "eu-central-1"
}
```

alex: Infra note: we can also pin KV cache and prefix cache to eu-central for the POC and ensure runtime logs are routed to EU-only observability. Customer-managed KMS keys are supported.

ops-bot: job #poc-largebank provision started by samir  creating resources in eu-central-1. ETA ~ 10m.

samir: I'll configure the hosted account with the snippet as default and prepare a Dedicated quote if they confirm SLA needs.

sara: Action items: (1) maria DM subprocessor CSV + SOC links to the customer legal; (2) diego update runbook and paste link here; (3) samir finalize Dedicated quote and include 2-week commitment option. I'll update the prospect.

maria: Sending CSV + SOC links now via DM.

diego: Runbook PR opened: https://git.internal/redwood/runbooks/poc-regional-pin (will paste final link).

samir: Quote drafted, putting on Sales template and will share before EOD.

sara: Thanks team 49A please ping here when all three are complete and I'll close the loop with LargeBank.
